item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This reflects my concerns as well. The fact that three advanced AI's are in a place that isn't a place, where, in theory, the only limits are the imaginations of the users isn't really addressed or used at all.

It feels as though the fact that you chose to do the Maxwellist city as a place with avatars and all that jazz was actually more narratively limiting than anything. Everything is basically the same as a story in meatspace, just with a few bits of flair to remind us that we're in cyberspace, where anything is possible. About halfway through, I began to wish that this had taken place in a MOO, where there is a long history of dealing with questions of selfhood, representation, and reality (NSFW/some secondhand accounts of sexual violence). This is just straightforward narrative, but also there are AIs and people can talk in emojis.

-1

It is probably just a matter of taste, but this virtual space is just way too much the Tron/Snow Crash kind, as it was imagined when people spoke of "cyberspace" in the 90s. It is, in a way, the most real space imaginable (since Second Life is just like that). I was just hoping the AIs would leave behind the 3D rendering space after Hello World 1 and end up in a less human-centric space.

I just really liked the official, serious tone of the paper establishing this MTF in part 1, but the actual individuals on the force and their adventures so far seem like they could happen in any setting.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm going to agree with what some others have said about characterization, but something else that also stood out to me was how bland the story currently is, for such a strong premise. Everything that seems like it would hurdle a straightforward story (and make it more interesting as a result!) is immediately bypassed.

The characters are AIs? Yeah, but they only act in cyberspace so it basically doesn't matter, they act like real people (except for the guy who can only say yes or no (who is also currently my favorite character)). The setting is a virtual maxwellist city? Yeah, but it's basically every single cyberpunk city you've ever seen, with some Second Life thrown in.

Right now, the only weirdness is on a conceptual level; the actual plot and characters reflect none. The characters try to blend in, jokes are made, people are weird, and then they enter into some contest to gain someone's trust (that certainly isn't a tired trope).

All that said: I'm still hoping this'll get really good. But currently, I'm finding it difficult to be engaged.
